implementerProof.how: Re-ran the implementer's 10x step three times at the same head on INFRA-589's harness (t-head-10x-a/b/c): 137-151 reads/s served (theirs 146.7), 80,202-82,744 reads and 6,742-6,778 writes refused 429 OVERLOADED (theirs 80,925 / 6,753), read refusal p50 16-18 ms p99 116-122 ms, 0 connection failures, at most 5 goroutines waiting for a pool connection. Their 1x step (t-head-1x-a) reproduced exactly: 0 refusals, 3.99 events/s committed, 1.16 request-pool checkouts per request. Their negative control reproduced on today's main (59f2ec9b): 10x 0 reads/s served, 107,347 reads timed out at 30 s, 19,740 goroutines waiting.

failures.criterion: The process exports pool size, in-use, waiting and acquire time per pool (spec acceptance line 4; the architect's check that /metrics names every pool with its waiters)
failures.evidence: Live scrape of 127.0.0.1:16062/metrics during t-head-1x-a lists 9 pools (requests, rooms, health, listen, leases, outbox, background, live, settlements) and no registry, while pg_stat_activity in the same stack shows a dispatch-registry connection, counted in store.ConnectionsPerProcess. The registry pool carries the heartbeat that keeps a serving process live (processes.Register opens it with pgxpool.NewWithConfig outside store.Pool, so store.Pool.Stats never reports it, though store/acquire.go poolNames lists RegistryPool); in the freeze run its heartbeat timed out 5 times and the process rejoined the registry, a wait no /metrics series showed. Red test: packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/metrics_test.go TestAServingProcessScrapeListsTheRegistryPool (commit 'test(dispatch): red test: a serving process's /metrics lists the registry pool'). It boots a real envoy-dispatch with DISPATCH_METRICS_ADDR and requires every per-pool series with pool="registry" and dispatch_db_pool_max_conns{pool="registry"} 1. Fails at the head: `cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://... go test ./cmd/dispatch/ -run TestAServingProcessScrapeListsTheRegistryPool -count=1` -> 8 lines 'the scrape has no line beginning "dispatch_db_pool_..._{pool=\"registry\"} "'; TestTheMetricsEndpointListsEverySeriesForEveryOpenPool passes beside it.

The check is not in main's required set (lint, typecheck, test, pr-title). At the time of reading, 'dispatch', 'envoy-go' and 'envoy-go-race' were still in progress; read as running.

observations: 1x without #2392 (#2392 still open): refused reads 0 / 165 / 36 of about 10,750 (0-1.53%), writes 0 / 34 / 36 of 720 (0-5.0%). The architect (Envoy 00:10Z) set the 1x band (0-0.1% reads, 0.7-1.5% writes) on #2402 merged after #2392 and asked these shares be recorded as measured.

The gate: a local merge of #2392's code head 38ee69626 into 6410259f (commit 09aad1cf in a scratch clone; conflicts in store/pool.go, api/events.go, api/event_stream_relay.go, api/delivery_live_hub_intake.go, docs/edit_notices.go resolved by folding #2392's horizon pool into #2402's named pools as 'horizon', 2 connections, budget 88): three 1x runs t-m2392-1x-a/b/c refused 0 reads and 0 writes, 3.99 of 3.99 events/s committed, read p99 247-282 ms. #2402's forward merge after #2392 will meet the same five conflicts and the budget moving to 88.
At 2x without #2392, 20-42% of writes are refused (293-605 of 1,440) and 4.62-6.36 of 8 events/s commit; the write class's 12 slots are full for the whole step.

CLI retry: the head's DispatchClient retries at most twice (RETRIES = 2). At 10x, where 75-77% of reads are refused, it recovered 76 of 170 refused reads and 94 failed after 3 attempts; at 2x it recovered 1 of 1 refused read and 31 of 40 refused writes (the write probe used the shared agent token without an actor, so an admitted retry answered 400 ACTOR_KIND: admission recovered, the write itself was refused by its own rule). Main's client recovered none.
One write refusal in t-head-10x-a took 6,293 ms (p99 1,126 ms) although admission's wait is 1 s; the refused body drain or a GC stall is the likely cause [INFERENCE, not traced].
pg_stat_activity under 10x shows 2 dispatch-listen connections, not the 3 permanent listeners ConnectionsPerProcess counts; the budget is an upper bound, so this is within it.
